raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll build a progressive 12-week upper-body–focused programme that respects the physio restriction: only pain-free range of motion, no loaded overhead work (no heavy pressing or loading with the arm elevated above ~90°). Because she’s a recreational climber and office worker, we’ll also include mobility, scapular control, rotator cuff and thoracic work, and climber-specific posterior chain and grip maintenance without aggravating the shoulder. Emphasis: build load tolerance gradually, prioritize pain-free movement quality, and respect the physio guidance (no overhead loading). I’ll assume she has had pain-free scapular/rotator cuff activation in physio and that a suitable warm-up is approved. If anything causes pain (sharp or increasing), stop that exercise and consult the physio.

Overview and progression
- Three phases, each 4 weeks: Re-establish control & load tolerance → Strength & stability → Strength to capacity and sport-transfer.
- Frequency: 3 gym sessions/week (upper-body focused). Two optional low-impact sessions (light lower-body/conditioning/climbing technique or soft bouldering within pain-free range) can be added later in Phase 2–3. Include daily short mobility/activation mini-sessions (5–10 min).
- Progression principle: start with low load, slow tempo, emphasis on scapular control and rotator cuff isometrics/low-load eccentrics. Increase load and complexity gradually; avoid overhead loaded pressing; substitute horizontal and low-angle vertical work, and use multiplanar scapular and rotator cuff strengthening.
- Return-to-climbing considerations: integrate sport-specific pulling & grip training only if shoulder remains pain-free. Avoid dynamic overhead reaching/lead-like moves until late Phase 3 and approved by physio.
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep, protein ~1.2–1.6 g/kg/day depending on goal, maintain hydration and anti-inflammatory nutrition patterns if needed. Use icing or soft tissue only as recommended by physio.

Terms and cues
- Pain-free range = movement within which the client experiences no sharp pain. Mild ache that settles after exercise can be tolerated only if cleared by physio.
- “No overhead loading” = avoid barbell/DB presses or loaded carries with arm >90° elevation. Cable/band rows, horizontal presses, low-incline presses up to ~45° are acceptable only if pain-free.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Control, scapular mechanics, rotator cuff tolerance
Goals: Re-establish scapular stability, rotator cuff endurance and thoracic mobility; reduce irritability; maintain posterior chain and grip for climbing.

Structure
- 3 sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri) — ~40–50 minutes.
- Daily 5–10 min morning activation: scapular retraction holds, wall slides (pain-free), doorway pec stretch if tight.

Session A — Scapular + Horizontal Strength
1. Warm-up (8–10 min)
   - Foam rolling upper back 2 min
   - Thoracic mobility: thoracic rotations on foam roller or seated windmills 1–2 min
   - Band pull-aparts (light, pain-free) 2 x 15 slow
2. Scapular/Rotator cuff activation
   - Prone Y/T/L on bench (Y = pain-free small range) 3 x 10 each, slow
   - Sidelying external rotation (neutral plane) 3 x 12 each side with light DB or band
   - Scapular protraction/retraction isometrics (standing) 3 x 10 s each
3. Strength (moderate reps, focus on control)
   - Seated row (neutral grip) 3 x 10–12, controlled 2:2
   - Incline dumbbell press (low incline ~15–30°) or chest press machine — keep elbows below shoulder plane and no elevation >90°: 3 x 10–12
   - Single-arm dumbbell row (supporting torso on bench) 3 x 10 each side
4. Accessory / climber-friendly
   - Face pulls (high but ensure pain-free: use band at chest-to-head height, emphasis on low-to-high scapular movement but avoid end-range elevation) 3 x 15
   - Farmer carry (light) 2 x 30–45 s (neutral shoulder)
5. Cool-down
   - Pec stretch, doorway 2 x 30 s
   - Gentle shoulder pendulum for 1–2 min if pain-free

Session B — Rotator Cuff Emphasis + Grip
1. Warm-up (as above)
2. Activation
   - Standing external rotation with band at elbow tucked (0–30° abduction) 3 x 15
   - Internal rotation with band 3 x 15
   - Scapular wall slides (pain-free, hands higher only as tolerated) 3 x 10
3. Strength / Pull emphasis
   - Lat pulldown to chest or neutral-grip pulldown (use light-moderate load; avoid reaching overhead if painful): 3 x 10–12
   - Chest-supported row (machine or incline bench row) 3 x 10–12
   - Horizontal TRX rows (body angle adjusted to control load) 3 x 8–12
4. Shoulder-friendly conditioning / grip
   - Deadlift variation (trap bar or kettlebell) 3 x 5–8 (maintain neutral shoulders; lower-body emphasis)
   - Towel holds or hang substitute: supported dead hang from a low bar with knees bent and feet on ground so shoulder not overloaded — 3 x 10–20 s, only if pain-free
5. Finisher / Mobility
   - Scapular clock (standing on all fours) 2 x 6 circles each direction
   - Soft tissue release of pec minor/major as tolerated

Session C — Stability & Posterior Chain
1. Warm-up
2. Activation
   - Serratus punches with band (low range) 3 x 12–15 (pain-free)
   - Isometric external rotation in 20–30° abduction (push into immovable object) 3 x 20 s
3. Strength
   - Chest press machine (neutral path) 3 x 10–12 (control)
   - Single-arm cable row, low-to-mid pulley (emphasize scapular squeeze) 3 x 10 each
   - Romanian deadlift (light–moderate) 3 x 8–10 (maintain posterior chain strength for climbing)
4. Accessory
   - Band pull-aparts 3 x 20
   - Eccentric-only negatives for external rotation: 3 x 8 each (very slow 4–5 s lowering) if tolerated
5. Cool-down
   - Gentle thoracic extension over foam roller 2 min

Progression notes for Phase 1:
- Weeks 1–2: use lighter loads, higher reps (10–15). Focus on pain-free perfect technique.
- Weeks 3–4: slightly increase load if all pain-free; progress rows/pulls in load; add 1–2 reps per set or an extra set for key exercises.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build strength and load tolerance (no overhead loaded pressing)
Goals: Increase strength of scapular stabilizers, rotator cuff, horizontal/low-angle pushing and pulling. Start sport-specific tensioning and grip work.

Structure
- 3 gym sessions/week. Add 1 optional light climbing technique or bouldering session mid-week if pain-free, limited to easy problems and no overhead dynos.

Session A — Horizontal Press & Pull
1. Warm-up + activation (10 min)
2. Strength
   - Flat DB bench press with neutral/supinated grip, elbows kept tucked (<60° abduction) 4 x 6–8 (increase load progressively but stop if any pain)
   - Bent-over single-arm row or supported DB row 4 x 6–8
   - Seated cable row (heavy) 3 x 8–10
3. Rotator cuff / scapula
   - Cuban press mimicked without elevation; better: upright band external rotation into scapular retraction 3 x 12
   - Face pulls 4 x 12–15
4. Grip/Climbing support
   - Repeaters on campus board or fingerboard? Only if fingerboard hangs are pain-free and shoulder comfortable — start with supported one-arm holds or assisted footed hangs: 3 x 5–10 s per grip type
   - Farmers carry heavier 3 x 30–45 s
5. Cool-down

Session B — Low- to Mid-angle Vertical Pull + Stability
1. Warm-up
2. Strength
   - Neutral-grip pulldown or pull-up progression (assisted) 4 x 6–8
   - Chest-supported incline row (45°) 3 x 8–10
   - Single-arm landmine row or low-cable high-row to chest height (emphasize scapular depression & retraction) 3 x 8 each
3. RCT / Scapula
   - Prone horizontal abduction (T) with moderate DBs 3 x 12
   - Serratus anterior dynamic push-up plus (wall → incline push-ups as tolerated) 3 x 8–10
4. Lower-body posterior chain maintenance (twice/week)
   - Single-leg Romanian deadlift 3 x 6–8 each
5. Conditioning: 10–15 min low-impact cardio

Session C — Mixed Strength + Eccentrics
1. Warm-up
2. Compound work
   - Cable chest press (mid-pulleys, approx 45°) 3 x 8–10 (keeps arms under 90°)
   - Heavy single-arm row 3 x 5–6
   - Kettlebell swings or deadlifts 3 x 8–10
3. Rotator cuff eccentrics & isometrics
   - Controlled eccentric external rotation 3 x 8
   - Isometric holds in neutral external rotation 3 x 20 s
4. Grip endurance
   - Towel rows or thick-bar holds 3 x 15–30 s
5. Mobility & soft tissue

Progression notes for Phase 2:
- Weeks 5–6: consolidate load; prioritize quality. Start increasing loads on horizontal pressing and pulling (lower-rep strength sets).
- Weeks 7–8: increase intensity (heavier loads, 4–6 reps on main lifts), but maintain pain-free range. Introduce more climbing-specific holds/hangs only if shoulder good.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Strength carryover and sport transfer
Goals: Increase maximal strength and integrate higher-tension climbing movements, plyometrics cautiously, and gradually reintroduce higher arm elevation activities in controlled ways if physio approves.

Structure
- 3 gym sessions/week; 1 optional light climbing session. Start integrating low-force overhead reaches (no loaded overhead) and scapular control in higher ranges.

Session A — Heavy Horizontal Strength & Pull
1. Warm-up + activation
2. Strength
   - Flat barbell or dumbbell press with controlled ROM (limit elevation; keep elbows tucked) 4 x 4–6
   - Weighted chin-up or heavy assisted pull-up 4 x 4–6 (neutral to supinated grip as tolerated)
   - Heavy single-arm row or T-bar row 4 x 4–6
3. RCT / scapula
   - Loaded serratus press with band 3 x 12
   - Face pulls 4 x 12
4. Grip power
   - Short max-effort hangs on fingerboard (4–6 s) with full foot assistance if needed: 4–6 hangs per session
5. Cool-down

Session B — Strength Endurance & Power Transfer
1. Warm-up
2. Strength/power
   - Explosive horizontal push (med ball chest pass) 3 x 6
   - Explosive rows (band-resisted row) 3 x 6–8
   - Romanian deadlifts / trap bar 4 x 4–6
3. Climbing-specific
   - Limit bouldering problems at V0–V2 to avoid risky overhead dynamic moves; focus on technique and footwork
   - Campus-style repeaters? Only if shoulder fully ready — otherwise continue fingerboard work as above
4. Accessory
   - Eccentric-loaded external rotation 3 x 6–8 slow
   - Scapular stability progressions (e.g., instability holds on Swiss ball) 3 x 30 s
5. Mobility

Session C — Mixed Capacity
1. Warm-up
2. Mixed lifts
   - Incline chest press (low incline) 3 x 6–8
   - Pulldown/pull-up variation 3 x 6–8
   - Farmer/carry variations 3 x 30–60 s
3. Conditioning: 15–20 min interval bike or row (low shoulder demand)
4. Finish with thoracic mobility and pec stretch

Progression notes for Phase 3:
- Weeks 9–10: Increase load and reduce reps on main lifts for strength.
- Weeks 11–12: Peak strength sets and return-to-sport work. If physio allows and the shoulder remains pain-free, begin low-load overhead work (band-resisted overhead reach, not loaded pressing) to test tolerance. Do not perform heavy overhead presses unless cleared.

Weekly sample schedule (example)
- Mon: Session A
- Tue: short mobility/activation 10 min + optional light bouldering/technique (Phase 2–3 only)
- Wed: Session B
- Thu: Active recovery / mobility / light cardio
- Fri: Session C
- Sat/Sun: one active day — hike/climb technique session that respects shoulder tolerance; Sunday rest

Exercise safety and red flags
- Stop any exercise that produces sharp, radiating, or progressively worsening pain.
- If she experiences night pain, sensory changes, or weakness increasing, refer to physio/MD immediately.
- Emphasize scapular control for all pulling and pushing: start movement with scapula (retract/depress) and avoid shrugging.

Nutrition & recovery recommendations
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day depending on body composition goals (higher if building strength/muscle).
- Calories: mild surplus for muscle gain (+200–300 kcal) or maintenance for strength without weight gain.
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours/night.
- Hydration: at least 2–2.5 L/day unless medical contraindication.
- Anti-inflammatory measures: keep inflammatory foods moderate; consider icing after sessions only if recommended by physio.
- Soft tissue care: pec minor release, thoracic mobilization, and posterior shoulder work 2–3x/week.

Return-to-climb milestones (suggested to discuss with physio)
- Phase 1 success: no provoked pain during activation & low-load rows; improved scapular control.
- Phase 2 success: heavy puling and horizontal pushing up to moderate load pain-free; start low-intensity climbing sessions.
- Phase 3 success: ability to perform heavier horizontal press/rows and short unweighted overhead reaches pain-free; progress to full climbing loads and overhead movements only if cleared.

Notes for you (trainer)
- Check in weekly about pain levels, sleep, and daily activities that might aggravate shoulder (desk posture).
- Make gradual weekly load adjustments (add 2–5% load or 1 rep) only when sessions are pain-free.
- Maintain communication with her physio for any progression into overhead loading or return-to-climb specifics.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this plan into a week-by-week printable calendar with specific loads (if you give current 1–5RM or conservative working weights).
- Provide a short daily 8–10 minute mobility & activation routine she can follow every morning.
- Tailor the plan to a specific climbing schedule (bouldering vs sport).

Would you like the week-by-week with specific sets/reps laid out as a calendar (weeks 1–12 listed explicitly) or target loading percentages for the strength lifts?
